classification.difficultyReason: Identify the two categories and translate the supplied 'all' or 'not all' wording into the corresponding directed subset relation.

content.prompt: Rewrite each statement by first describing the two sets and writing the symbol $\subseteq$ or $\nsubseteq$ between them.

answer.worked:
Every fish is an animal, so every element of the first set belongs to the second set.

$\{\text{fish}\}\subseteq\{\text{animals}\}$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Numbers ending in 6 are all even.

answer.worked:
Every number in the first set is even, so it belongs to the second set.

$\{\text{numbers ending in }6\}\subseteq\{\text{even numbers}\}$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Not all children with blonde hair are naughty.

answer.worked:
The statement says that at least one child with blonde hair is not naughty. Therefore, at least one element of the first set is outside the second set.

$\{\text{children with blonde hair}\}\nsubseteq\{\text{naughty people}\}$

children.label: d
children.prompt: Not all numbers ending in 4 are multiples of 4.

answer.worked:
The statement says that at least one number ending in 4 is not a multiple of 4. Therefore, the first set is not a subset of the second set.

$\{\text{numbers ending in }4\}\nsubseteq\{\text{multiples of }4\}$
